A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, 37-page versions of the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, checklist, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original control-task experiments with VI-TD3, VI-SAC, and VI-TD7, plus ablations and a toy-grid experiment in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains the original control-task experiments, ablations, and toy-grid results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4, explicit policy-gradient and Best-of-N improvement, implicit expectile improvement, and network architectures are unchanged. Revised policy-iteration terminology does not alter the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 DeepMind Control tasks and the same toy-grid scenario in Appendix B.5. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The TD3/SAC comparisons in Figure 3, TD7 comparison in Figure 5, and acting-policy and replay-ratio controls in Figures 6–7 retain the same participants. The added Uni-RL citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, greedification settings, model configurations, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix D.3 still specifies three evaluation episodes every 5,000 interactions, using policy means for action selection.

E4.justification: Both retain the greedification sweeps, overestimation analysis, acting-policy update and replay-ratio ablations, and comparison of value versus policy improvement in Figures 1–2 and 4–8.

E5.justification: Seed counts and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Figure 3 still uses 10 seeds for BoN and 20 for other agents with two standard errors; the appendix figures retain their existing reporting practices.

E6.justification: All eight figures retain identical drawing content, and Table 1 retains every numerical entry. For example, the humanoid-stand maximum performance gain remains 503.93 ± 14.72 at τ = 0.75.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, convergence theorems, corollaries, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Section 2 reorganizes the existing Bellman-update explanation without changing the formal setup or proof arguments.

C1.justification: The claims about decoupling acting and evaluated policies, finite-horizon convergence under sufficient greedification, and TD3/SAC performance remain unchanged. The revised abstract makes the already-present approximate-evaluation framework more explicit.

C2.justification: The greedification–stability and overestimation interpretations remain unchanged, as do the theoretical applicability limits and Appendix D.2's warning about risk-seeking behavior in stochastic environments.

D1.justification: v4 adds a specific code repository address in footnote 1. v3 only states that supplementary materials contain code and instructions. Appendix D's implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Xu et al. (2025), Uni-RL, to the conclusion and references. Section 5's substantive discussion remains unchanged. Other bibliography edits, including Huang et al.'s publication update, concern already-cited works.

P1.justification: v4 expands Section 2's policy-iteration explanation, introduces more explicit approximate-policy-iteration terminology, and lightly rewrites the abstract and conclusion. Bibliographic wording is also edited; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from page 4 to 5, Figure 1 from page 7 to 8, and Figure 3 from page 8 to 9. Table 1's caption expands 'overest.' to 'overestimation'; plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new explicit repository address improves code discoverability, while Section 2 explains the existing policy-iteration framework more clearly. These are modest documentation and readability gains; the algorithms, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
